## 3. Monitoring, functioning and control

### 3.1 Logging (Article 12 and Article 19)

*Observed.* Flugschreiber records one structured, hash-chained event per model
interaction. Over the evidence window it captured:

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Total records | 5 |
| Inference events | 5 |
| Distinct calling identities | 3 (recorded as salted hashes, not credentials) |
| Distinct sessions | 3 |
| Requests with errors | 1 (20%) |
| Prompt tokens | 826 |
| Completion tokens | 432 |
| Median end-to-end latency | 812.4 ms |
| 95th percentile latency | 2240.9 ms |
| Event types recorded | inference (5) |
| HTTP status codes | 200 (4), 503 (1) |
| Finish reasons | stop (2), tool_calls (1) |

Each record carries: an RFC3339 timestamp, a monotonic sequence number, request and
session identifiers, the requested and served model, the endpoint and upstream, generation
parameters, token usage, latency, HTTP status, a salted hash of the calling identity, and
the content record described in 3.2.

> **TODO:** Article 12 asks for logs appropriate to the intended purpose. Confirm that the fields above are sufficient for your use case, and record here anything you log elsewhere that Flugschreiber does not see, for example application-level user identity, or the retrieval documents injected into a prompt.

### 3.2 What is recorded of the content itself

*Observed.* The active content mode is **`hash`**.
Modes seen across the recorded window: hash (5).

- `hash`: a SHA-256 of the exact request and response bytes is recorded; no prompt or
  completion text is retained. This is the default, chosen for GDPR Article 5(1)(c) data
  minimisation: a proxy that stores every prompt by default would create a new copy of
  whatever users type, in a system that was not designed to hold it.
- `redact`: text is retained with configured patterns replaced.

  Pattern-based redaction is best-effort by nature; free text can carry personal data in
  forms no regular expression will match.
- `store`: full request and response text is retained.

In every mode the SHA-256 is computed over the complete bytes that crossed the wire. That
is what lets a transcript held elsewhere be proven to be the transcript of the interaction
this log attests to, even when the log itself holds no text.

> **TODO:** Record why the chosen content mode is appropriate here, and where the corresponding retention and access controls are documented.

### 3.3 Retention

*Observed.* Configured retention: **180 days** (~6.0 months).

Article 19 expects automatically generated logs to be kept for at least six months where
they are under the provider's control, subject to other applicable law. Flugschreiber
refuses to start with a retention setting below 180 days.

> **TODO:** Record where the evidence directory is stored, who can read it, how it is backed up, and what happens at the end of the retention period. Retention enforcement and legal hold are configured but not yet automated by this version, so deletion is currently your operational responsibility.

### 3.4 Integrity mechanism

*Observed.* Every record carries the SHA-256 of its predecessor and a SHA-256 of its own
contents, forming a chain. Altering, inserting or removing any record breaks the chain at
that point and at every point after it.

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verification result | **intact**, every record hash and link verified |
| Segments | 1 (seg-00000001.jsonl) |
| Chain head hash | `b7b7feea6202d55ad35f83ff5c763fa29151c9a450efcecd06b5becd39ead10c` |
| Verified at | 2026-05-04T09:00:00Z |

Anyone can re-run this check against the evidence directory with:

```
flugschreiber verify --dir <evidence-directory>
```

The verifier reads only the files on disk. It needs no running server and no access to
your infrastructure, so the check can be repeated by an auditor holding nothing but a copy
of the log.

> **TODO:** This version chains records but does not yet sign checkpoints. Until signed checkpoints ship, the chain proves internal consistency. It detects modification of the log, but someone with write access to the whole directory could in principle rewrite it end to end. Record what protects the directory itself: append-only storage, write-once object locks, off-host replication, or restricted filesystem permissions.

## Appendix A: regulatory timeline

Dates reflect the timeline following the Digital Omnibus agreement. Verify against the
current text before relying on them.

| Date | What applies |
| --- | --- |
| 2 August 2026 | Article 50 transparency obligations |
| 2 December 2026 | New prohibitions |
| 2 December 2027 | Annex III high-risk obligations |
| 2 August 2028 | Annex I obligations |

Within the first row, one duty starts later: the machine-readable marking in
Article 50(2) applies from 2 December 2026 for systems already on the market on
2 August 2026. The interaction disclosure in Article 50(1) is not deferred.
